messages:
mira: quick idea: instead of packing all warmup hints into immutable safetensors header, what if we split into tiny immutable base + a mutable sidecar that can carry per-deployment deltas? pros/cons?
anika: sidecar = nice for iterative profiling. you can bump priorities post-publish without repacking weights. downside: private/on-prem needs a way to host sidecar or we force it to be embedded.
rohan: for private deployments we could let infra mount a local sidecar store (S3-like) or allow embedding during import. but that adds operational surface.
evans: how would runtime merge header+sidecar? precedence rules? atomicity? we need to avoid inconsistent views mid-warmup.
mira: plan: header contains base_priority (uint8 per chunk) + per-chunk crc32. sidecar contains delta_priority adjustments + signed timestamp. runtime: read header, then attempt to fetch sidecar; if sidecar exists and signature verifies, merge by per-chunk add-with-saturation. merge must be atomic from runtime perspective: load both before starting prefetch.
kevin: can we reuse existing registry signing for sidecar? else we'd need new key mgmt. registry-signed sidecars only for hosted. fall back to unsigned in private. we should detect unsigned+prod and disable sidecar there.
anika: security note: sidecar opens a vector for IO amplification if untrusted. require per-sidecar attest or limit prefetches for unsigned sidecars.
rohan: operational limit: also need cross-host coherence when sidecar updates. use versioned sidecar keys (v1, v2) and epoch in response to avoid thrash.
evans: what about bandwidth and prefetch budget? We should cap prefetch by both per-request chunk limit and a concurrent_host_warmup_budget to avoid domino effect. suggest defaults: per-request 16 chunks, host concurrency budget 256 chunks.
mira: agreed. we'll expose these as runtime configs with safe defaults. metrics will drive tuning.
kevin: telemetry: track sidecar_present (true|false), sidecar_signed (true|false), warmup_merge_mode (header-only|sidecar-merged), chunk_prefetch_count, chunk_miss_after_warmup. we also need IO_thrash_rate alert if read amplification spikes.
anika: acceptance criteria for rollout: p95 inference latency improves by >3% on a selected model family in canary without IO_thrash_rate > baseline*1.2 and error rate stable.
rohan: benchmark idea: spin up a microbench that simulates common prompt shapes and compare index-first vs header-only vs header+sidecar. measure token-latency & bytes-read.
evans: implementation sketch: add SidecarProvider interface with two impls: RegistrySidecarFetcher (signed, cached) and LocalSidecarFile (for on-prem). runtime will call provider.resolve(model_id)->Optional(sidecar_blob). sidecar_blob schema: version, epoch, delta_bytes (base64).
mira: small example sidecar payload: ```
version: 1
epoch: 2026-03-01T12:00:00Z
deltas: base64(Uw==) // bytes per chunk signed int8
signature: "..."
```
kevin: keep base64 compact. deltas length must equal chunks count. document strict length checks and crc32 cross-checks.
anika: fallback policy: if sidecar present but fails signature/length checks, runtime logs and continues with header-only. if header missing, fallback to index-first. always avoid throwing inference errors for missing metadata.
mira: good. also add migration note: when publishing new bundles, model builders should optionally emit both header and sidecar; for old bundles, sidecar-only publishing should be supported with a small shim that publishes a stub header during registry ingest.
rohan: ops question: who hosts sidecar for multi-region? replicate sidecars in registry per-region or use CDN. prefer registry-replicated artifacts to minimize cross-region latency.
evans: dev ergonomics: add a CLI `rw-weights sidecar apply --model MODEL --file sidecar.json --signed` to push to registry. that helps SEs iterate.
kevin: I'm volunteering to write the sidecar schema + validator and add a note to the safetensors extension RFC about sidecar semantics.
anika: I'll write the telemetry dashboards and alert rules. rohan can prototype the RegistrySidecarFetcher behavior. evan will add runtime knobs and safe defaults.
jax-bot: deploy-bot: opened ticket RW-ml/2491: "sidecar metadata for warmup deltas + runtime merge rules"
mira: TL;DR: propose hybrid model: small immutable warmup baseline in header (crc32 included) + optional signed mutable sidecar for deployment-specific tuning. runtime merges atomically, bounded prefetch, signed-sidecar required in prod; fallback to header/index-first for legacy.
evans: sounds good. next step: owners doc + small PoC benchmark.
kevin: will add owners in the ticket.
rohan: bye folks.
